question: A 55-year-old man has well-controlled type 2 diabetes on oral medication, mild hypertension on a single drug, and exercises without limitation. He is scheduled for elective inguinal hernia repair. What is his ASA physical status classification?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: ASA I applies to a completely healthy patient. This patient has two controlled systemic diseases.

answers.text: ASA II — mild systemic disease with no functional limitation

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Well-controlled diabetes and mild hypertension on single-drug therapy, with no functional limitation (exercises without limitation), constitute mild systemic disease — ASA II.

answers.text: ASA III — severe systemic disease limiting activity

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: ASA III requires substantive functional limitation. This patient has no exercise limitation, so his controlled comorbidities are class II.
ASA IV is reserved for patients with life-threatening systemic disease such as recent MI, severe heart failure, or end-stage renal failure.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review ASA classification: ASA I = healthy; ASA II = mild controlled disease, no functional limit; ASA III = severe disease, activity limited; ASA IV = life-threatening disease. Controlled DM + hypertension without limitation = ASA II.
Correct. ASA II = mild systemic disease without functional limitation. Remember that ASA grades comorbidity burden, while Mallampati grades airway difficulty — these are independent assessments.
